headline: Capitol Center for the Arts theater addition at 44 South Main Street approved
summary: The approved plan adds a fully accessible elevator to all floors, a covered canopy on the north side, and a new marquee and signs. A conditional use permit for a wall sign above 25 feet will be considered at the December 16th meeting. Brixmor's plan to split the former Joann Fabrics space at 80 Storrs Street into five units was also approved. Signature Homes presented a 59-unit development on Sonoma Lane, and its design review phase was closed.
decisions: Approved design review items 5A through 5G together, by consent, with design review recommendations.
Continued the major site plan and conditional use permit for 52 Locke Road to the December 16th, 2026 meeting, at the applicant's request.
Approved a conditional use permit for a pet grooming salon at 85 Manchester Street.
Recommended that the city council allow building permits on Peaceful Lane, a private road.
Approved a minor subdivision for a lot line adjustment between 110 and 114 Peaceful Lane.
Approved a major site plan for an approximately 1,830 ft² mail center at 7 Rectory Road.
Approved a minor subdivision for a lot line adjustment between 56 and 60 Bow Street, with the changes noted by staff.
Approved a minor site plan for a 4,200-square-foot addition to the theater at 44 South Main Street.
Approved an amended plan for five new parking lot light poles at 52 to 54 Portsmouth Street.
Approved a conditional use permit for 769 parking spaces where 1,247 are required, at 80 Storrs Street.
Approved a minor site plan to split the former Joann Fabrics space at 80 Storrs Street into five units.
Continued the amendment for decorative building lighting at 80 Storrs Street to the December 16th, 2026 meeting.
Determined the design review phase complete for the 59-unit Sonoma Lane development.
discussion: Capitol Center stormwater waiver: The staff report did not support the stormwater waiver. The applicant said the site is too small for a stormwater system, and runoff would go into the city pipe. Members said the added flow is small.

80 Storrs Street parking: Members asked about parking and enforcement at the shopping center. Brixmor said a private company now enforces parking, and some retail tenants want assurance that parking will not be a problem.

Storrs Street decorative lights: The design review board asked for the tower lights to run at 20 percent and for more information on brightness. The lights were built without a dimmer, and the lights will stay off if one cannot be installed.
Sonoma Lane roundabouts and lighting: The applicant will meet with staff and a traffic engineer before discussing roundabouts. The applicant agreed to add light poles like those at Tuscany Village.
Mail center curbing: Members discussed the curb near the parking spaces. The applicant said the concrete slab would act as monolithic curbing, and the approval was changed to allow it.
